content_voiceover: Follicular lymphoma has a median age of about sixty and, interestingly, is less common in Asian and African American populations compared to Caucasians, a demographic point that occasionally shows up on exams. Biologically it's extremely sensitive to both radiation and chemotherapy, which is why localized disease can sometimes be cured with radiation alone. There's a notable association with hepatitis C infection, and in those patients, treating the underlying hepatitis C with interferon and ribavirin can actually induce lymphoma regression. Clinically, patients present with lymphadenopathy, but B symptoms like fever, night sweats, and weight loss are uncommon, seen in only about ten percent. Splenomegaly is present in roughly half of patients. The molecular hallmark is the t 14;18 translocation involving BCL2, found in about eighty-five percent of cases, leading to BCL2 overexpression and resistance to apoptosis. Despite this, only fifteen to thirty percent of patients present with early stage, localized disease, most present with advanced stage at diagnosis. The immunophenotype is CD10 positive, BCL2 positive, BCL6 positive, CD20 positive, with CD23 variable, and importantly CD43 negative and CD5 negative, which helps distinguish it from mantle cell and CLL slash SLL.
keypoints: Median age ~60; less common in Asian and African American patients
Highly radiosensitive and chemosensitive; hepatitis C linked, responds to IFN/ribavirin
t(14;18) BCL2 translocation in ~85% of cases
Only 15-30% present at early stage; splenomegaly in ~50%
Immunophenotype: CD10+, BCL2+, BCL6+, CD20+, CD5-, CD43-
keypoint_voiceover: Follicular lymphoma presents around age sixty, is highly sensitive to radiation and chemo, and has a hepatitis C association that can respond to antiviral therapy. The molecular hallmark is t 14;18 with BCL2 in about eighty-five percent of cases. Most patients present with advanced, not early, stage disease. And remember the immunophenotype, CD10 positive, BCL2 positive, BCL6 positive, but CD5 and CD43 negative, distinguishing it from mantle cell lymphoma.
